hook: US workers got more done with barely any extra hours in Q3 2026, sparking fresh arguments over AI's role in the surge.
name: US Productivity Hits Strongest Gain in a Year as AI Debate Rages
summary: Nonfarm business labor productivity rose at a 3.6% annualized rate in the third quarter, the strongest in a year, with output up 3.7% while hours worked increased just 0.1%. Economists split on causes: Apollo Global sees no broad AI boost beyond tech giants, while Stanford's Erik Brynjolfsson points to the sharp rise as evidence supporting his productivity growth bet. Factors like post-pandemic policies and labor shifts may contribute, as AI adoption remains uneven across firms.

hook: British employees are stepping back from extra effort at work, sticking to paid duties while chasing better balance. Data reveals this shift has grown real over the past decade.
name: British Workers Pull Back Effort Amid Falling Job Satisfaction
summary: A Resolution Foundation analysis of the British Social Attitudes survey shows the share of workers willing to go beyond basics dropped from 69% in 2015 to 55% in 2025, with job satisfaction hitting a 35-year low of 74%. Stagnant real wages since 2008, now around £589 weekly, high taxes, and fading perks fuel the change, often called quiet quitting. Think tank economist Hannah Slaughter warns this dissatisfaction hurts workers and threatens productivity and living standards, as fewer adults—especially men—seek full-time roles.
